origins.section: One SimpleDateFormat Shared by Threads Returns Wrong Dates
A Date Has No Zone; toString() Uses the JVM's Default
A Date Is a Mutable Moment, So Anyone Holding It Can Move It
java.sql.Date Is a java.util.Date That Breaks Its Parent's Contract

recorded.prompt:q-static-formatter: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-static-formatter: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-static-formatter: Page: 'A SimpleDateFormat keeps a Calendar and a DecimalFormat in instance fields and uses them as scratch space on every parse, so concurrent parses overwrite each other's partial results. ... most failures return a date, another thread's or a mix that nobody passed in, and nothing logs them.' Decides c.
recorded.prompt:q-two-servers-log: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-servers-log: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-two-servers-log: 'A Date holds one long, milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00Z'; 'Both JVMs hold the same getTime(). toString() ... use the JVM's default zone.' Same pattern as the page's example. Decides b (the reader must do the offset arithmetic).
recorded.prompt:q-final-due-date: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-final-due-date: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-final-due-date: 'final fixes which object the field points to, not what is inside it. The getter handed out the meeting's own object, so the reminder service moved the meeting itself.' Decides c.
recorded.prompt:q-distinct-days: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-distinct-days: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-distinct-days: 'The constructor keeps the time of day and equals compares getTime(), so two values that print the same day aren't equal, and a Set of them keeps both.' Decides d.
